title: Restricted total-limit comparison with adjunction projections
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ have inverse image on underlying sheaves the constant sequence, with ring map given by $A\to B_n$. Let $U:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A)))$ be termwise restriction of scalars. There is a specified natural comparison $Rp_*\cong\mathcal L=R\lim\,U$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] preserving actual total-limit projections $\pi_n:\mathcal L N\to\operatorname{Res}_nN_n$. Transport the adjunction $\mathcal R=Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction] along this comparison. Its unit $u_P:P\to\mathcal L\mathcal R P$ has nth projection the reduction unit, and its counit $e_N:\mathcal R\mathcal L N\to N$ has nth component the derived scalar-extension adjunct of $\pi_n$. Thus the adjoint of $h:P\to\mathcal L N$ has component $e_{N,n}\circ(h\otimes_A^LB_n)$. The triangle identities hold in the actual derived categories.

source.place: Tags 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok) and 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); agent tracks the actual projections through the canonical resolution comparisons.

proof.text: Take the normalized ordinary and derived sequence adjunction. The universal property of its compatible-family right adjoint identifies it naturally with lim after the actual restricted-tower functor U0, preserving every ordinary projection. Restriction is exact by the restricted-resolution lemma. The constant-coefficient total-limit theorem supplies the universal right derived pair (RL, etaLim). Derive each ordinary limit projection by the universal right-derived descent property.

Construct delta: Q F -> Q U0^D RL by the ordinary limit isomorphism, etaLim and the exact restriction factorization. For K-injective I resolve U0 I by T. The restricted-resolution lemma makes lim(j) a quasi-isomorphism, so naturality and the computation of etaLim on T show delta_I invertible. Strict systems are Grothendieck abelian; the K-injective derivability criterion makes delta universal. Uniqueness of right derived functors yields c:R -> U0^D RL with eta c=delta. Naturality gives the required explicit resolution equation.

Localize the exact comparison U0 followed by evaluation = system evaluation followed by restriction. The resulting xi is normalized by the exact-factor isomorphisms. Substitute eta c=delta and use naturality of the derived limit projection, cancellation of the restriction factor isomorphism, and the ordinary projection equation. This proves the asserted compatibility with the actual projections on every complex.

Transport the normalized scalar model adjunction along the given isomorphism from evaluation of G to sheafified scalar extension. Its pure-tensor formula is unchanged. Maps out of scalar extension are determined by local unit tensors, so the level transpose of the evaluated ordinary counit is exactly the ordinary limit projection.

Use flat-term K-flat resolutions to show the universal left derived sequence functor remains universal after exact evaluation or postcomposition by any functor: on the homotopy category the resolving diagrams are essentially constant, hence their defining right Kan extensions are absolute. Transfer this through the cochain-homotopy comparison. Derive the level adjunction to exact scalar restriction and normalize its Hom equivalence on every cochain map.

Transport the sequence adjunction through c. The natural transformation whose component is the level adjoint of the evaluated derived counit agrees with the total-limit projection: by the right-derived universal property it suffices to precompose with delta on all complexes, where the normalized Hom formulas and the ordinary counit projection prove the equality. The unit projection follows by transposing and applying the left triangle. The inverse adjunct formula is functoriality applied to L(h) followed by the counit. Both triangle identities hold for the transported adjunction.
